title: Predictable tail latency investigations and quantile action runbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Title: Predictable tail latency investigations and quantile action runbook

Short summary:
This runbook defines a step-by-step investigation and mitigation procedure for persistent or recurring tail latency (95th-99.9th quantiles) degradations in model inference services. It focuses on quickly identifying whether the cause is: request patterns, model hotset/kv-cache behavior, batch scheduler anomalies, kernel stalls on GPUs, network saturation, or tenant-induced contention. It assumes SLOs defined per-service and per-tenant.

Scope:
- Applies to model inference frontends, batchers, and GPU worker pools.
- Covers degradations that manifest in p95, p99, and p99.9 latency metrics lasting > 5 minutes or repeated across multiple deploys.
- Excludes systemic cloud provider outages (follow cloud incident runbook).

Owner and contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-sre - Model Serving Reliability
- On-call: inference-sre@redwood.ai
- Escalation: Runtime team pager -> runtime-lead@redwood.ai

SLOs and metrics referenced:
- request_latency_seconds{quantile="0.95|0.99|0.999"} (histogram_quantile)
- request_tokens_per_second
- batch_size_distribution
- gpu_kernel_time_ms
- kv_cache_miss_rate
- host_cpu_util, host_mem_free, net_interface_drops
- tenant_throttle_events

Observable signals and quick checks (in order):
1) Validate the symptom window
   - Query: PromQL examples
     - p99 over window: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))
     - p99.9: histogram_quantile(0.999, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))
2) Check deployment and release events in last 30 minutes (CI/CD webhook, release pipeline)
3) Inspect request-rate changes: spike, burst, or slow steady increase
4) Check batcher queue length and batch-size skew
5) Verify KV cache health: miss-rate and hot-key pressure
6) GPU telemetry: kernel stalls, SM utilization mismatch, CUDA errors
7) Network: interface errors, retransmits, cross-AZ latency
8) Tenant signals: token-priority shifts, quota exhaustion, sudden large embedding requests

Investigation procedure (step-by-step):
1) Triage (first 5–15 minutes)
   - Confirm affected services and tenant scope (global, regional, single-tenant).
   - If only p95 increased but p99 stable, prioritize request shaping and burst smoothing.
   - If p99/p99.9 increased, treat as possible serialization / hardware stall / cold-start
   - Collect evidence snapshot: traces (full traces for samples), top 100 slow tokens, sampling of requests.

2) Correlate with recent changes (5–60 minutes)
   - Check rollout history and model-variant switches.
   - Query A/B logs: are canary nodes affected disproportionately?
   - Review autoscaler events and recent scale downs that may have drained warm pools.

3) Isolate subsystem
   - Temporarily route a small fraction of traffic to known-good model-variant or older revision.
   - If latency recovers on fallback, capture comparative traces and stop rollout.

4) Deep-dive telemetry (if simple mitigations fail)
   - Batcher-level: inspect queue histograms, per-worker batch-size variance, and batch formation latency.
   - KV-cache-level: run memcached/redis slowlog and check connection errors.
   - GPU-level: run nv-smi diagnostics, collect coredump if OOM or GPU driver error.
   - OS-level: check dmesg for kernel watchdogs, GPU stalls, or RDMA errors.

Fast mitigations (prioritize least-disruptive):
1) Add capacity to worker pool (warm pool scale up):
   - kubectl scale deployment/<worker> --replicas=<+N>
   - OR increase reserved GPU nodes via autoscaler override in the short term
2) Reduce batching window and enforce max batch size:
   - Adjust batcher config: max_latency_ms=10 -> 5, max_batch_size=32 -> 16
3) Apply tenant-level throttles to noisy tenants (token-based priority):
   - Activate temporary token-priority caps via traffic-gating API
4) Rollback recent model variant or kernel patch

Remediation and follow-up actions:
- If root cause is algorithmic (model sequence length changes), update model-serving configuration: adjust kv_cache prefetch, max_seq_length policy, and batcher timeouts.
- If hardware-related, schedule node replacement and file incident with hardware vendor. Attach nv-logs and core dumps.
- If caused by tenant behavior, add workload-specific autoscaling rules and tenant quotas; inform customer success for high-impact tenants.

Decision matrix: when to declare incident and escalate
- Declare Sev-1 if p99.9 > 3x SLO for > 15 minutes and > 10% of requests affected.
- Declare Sev-2 if p99 > 2x SLO for > 30 minutes.
- Escalate to platform engineering when mitigation requires kernel or driver-level rollback.

Dashboards and queries to include in incident packet:
- Service latency heatmap by deployment (last 1h)
- Top trace spans contributing to p99
- Batch-size vs latency scatterplot
- KV cache miss-rate timeline
- GPU kernel stall events timeline

Tables: SLO thresholds and suggested immediate action
| Quantile | Threshold (example) | Immediate action |
| p95 | 200 ms | Reduce batching window; enable soft-throttle |
| p99 | 500 ms | Add warm-capacity; scale up batch workers |
| p99.9 | 2 s | Route to fallback model variant; initiate incident |

Incident review checklist (post-incident):
1) Produce a timeline with annotated signals and operator actions.
2) Attach sample traces (good vs bad) and batcher histograms.
3) Confirm permanent fix: configuration change, code patch, capacity adjustment, or customer limit.
4) Measure regression: rerun synthetic canaries and ensure p99 within SLO for 72 hours.
5) Update runbook with new detection rules and rerun chaos-tests to validate.

Automated tooling and playbooks to build:
- p99.9 auto-sample tracer capture and store for 24 hours after detection
- Automatic fallback routing when p99.9 crosses emergency threshold
- Batcher-sim replay harness to reconstruct skewed batch formation

Ownership and review cadence:
- Runbook owner: Model Serving SRE (Aisha Patel)
- Quarterly review: include runtime and serving teams; update thresholds when models or infra change
- Runbook exercise: schedule annual tabletop & chaos-testing against slow-paths

Appendix: example PromQL snippets and CLI commands
- p99 PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))
- Batch queue length: sum(rate(batcher_queue_length[1m])) by (worker)
- NV diagnostics: /usr/local/bin/nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv
- Example traffic-shaping curl: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"tenant":"TID","max_tokens_per_min":10000}' https://controlplane.internal/traffic-gating
